judged_text: The new specs cover only the settings gating and stub out the behavior the feature actually adds — poll_feed's URL fallback, entity unescaping and TopicEmbed.import call, plus TopicEmbed.import_remote and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve/fetch_http, have zero coverage. A regression in the feed import loop (such as the nil-content crash or an escaping change) breaks feed importing with no failing spec, and because the job is scheduled with retry: false nothing in CI or production surfaces it until operators notice their feed silently stopped importing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS parsing, link/id fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls) and in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve/#fetch_http` plus `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (HTTP fetch + Readability). However, the added specs largely only cover settings gating/stubbing: `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` tests only `execute` preconditions and never exercises `poll_feed`; `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` asserts `perform_retrieve` is/waswo not called and stubs `retrieved_recently?`, without covering `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`; `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` mocks `TopicRetriever` instead of running it; and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` covers `.import` but not `.import_remote`. So regressions in the feed import loop or retrieval path would not be caught by CI, which is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than an already-broken behavior.
